candidates.name: jsonwebtoken 11.0.0 with aws_lc_rs
candidates.fit_for_gap: Selects exactly one built-in provider for the existing direct jsonwebtoken 11 API while reusing aws-lc-rs already active in the server-full graph.
candidates.license: MIT; backend ISC AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC)

evidence.claim: Upstream merged CryptoProvider with built-in AWS-LC and RustCrypto backends and support for selective custom composition.
Non-FIPS AWS-LC supports and tests the Linux, macOS, and Windows targets in UAR's release matrix and requires only a C/C++ compiler.

The pinned crate exposes aws_lc_rs as one of exactly two built-in provider features. Read-only feature simulation left the active normal/build package count at the 918-package baseline and produced no manifest or lockfile diff.
The inspected 2026 aws-lc-sys advisory is patched from 0.38.0; UAR currently locks 0.41.0.

risks: C, assembly, and FFI remain part of the trusted native dependency surface.
This ordinary backend is non-FIPS and must not be reported as a FIPS configuration.
A future no_std, bare-WASM, or C/C++-free target would invalidate the portability fit.
candidates.decision_rationale: Adopt for server-full because it fixes the observed provider panic, matches RustCrypto's JWT algorithm coverage, supports every release target, and measured feature simulation adds zero active packages while preserving the locked graph.

candidates.name: jsonwebtoken 11.0.0 with rust_crypto
candidates.fit_for_gap: Selects a pure-Rust built-in provider with the required JWT algorithms and broader no_std/WASM portability.

evidence.claim: RustCrypto supplies the pure-Rust RSA component used by jsonwebtoken's rust_crypto backend.
Read-only feature simulation increased active normal/build packages from 918 to 940. The 22-package set difference includes ed25519-dalek, p256, p384, and rsa 0.9.10.
The RSA Marvin timing advisory lists no patched version and concerns remotely observable private-key timing leakage.

risks: Expands the active server-full dependency graph despite the packages already appearing in Cargo.lock.
Activates rsa 0.9.10 while its private-key timing advisory has no patched stable version, although no current UAR RS/PS signing path was observed.
Its principal portability benefits do not satisfy a current certified server-full requirement.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reject as UAR's server-full standard backend. It is functionally valid, but it measurably activates 22 additional packages while its portability advantages are out of scope; the RSA advisory is a secondary consideration.

candidates.name: Manual custom jsonwebtoken CryptoProvider
candidates.fit_for_gap: Could install a process-level provider or compose per-algorithm implementations without selecting a built-in feature.

evidence.claim: The custom-provider use case was resolved by upstream CryptoProvider support, primarily for requirements such as HSMs or alternate signers/verifiers.
Manual installation is process-global and succeeds at most once; a built-in feature performs the required selection without runtime initialization code.

risks: Adds source-level initialization ordering and a process-global correctness surface.
Creates unsupported provider composition without an HSM, KMS, or missing-algorithm requirement.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reject because the observed failure is fully solved by one built-in feature and no custom-cryptography requirement exists.
